models.title: Duration-convexity price change approximation
models.summary: Expected price change from a yield shift as duration plus convexity terms.

relationship.original_equation: E(ΔPrice based on views of yields) = (−ModDur × ΔYield) + [½ × Convexity × (ΔYield)²]
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Views of Benchmark Yields, printed p. 67 (PDF p. 77); Smith example (−3.70 × 0.0026) + [½ × 18 × (0.0026)²] = −0.0096
relationship.translation_notes: First-order Taylor (duration) plus second-order (convexity) terms of the price–yield curve; for embedded options use effective duration/convexity (per source). 0.5 is the Taylor-series constant (pure arithmetic literal). Decimal form throughout. Dimensional check: (1 × dimensionless) + (dimensionless × dimensionless) = dimensionless fractional change.

variables.definition: Modified (or effective, for embedded options) duration
variables.context: same bond or portfolio and yield shift as dy

variables.definition: Expected change in yield to maturity, in decimal form (signed)
variables.context: same bond or portfolio and horizon as md

variables.definition: Convexity statistic on the same scaling as the duration (raw, undivided) so the ½·C·(Δy)² term is consistent
variables.context: same bond or portfolio and horizon as md

variables.source_symbol: E(ΔPrice based on investor's views of yields)
variables.definition: Expected fractional price change from the yield view, in decimal form (signed)
variables.context: same bond or portfolio and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Yield shift is modest so the second-order expansion summarizes the price–yield curve (per source limitations).
Convexity scaling matches the duration measure (raw statistic; vendor-divided-by-100 figures must be rescaled first, per source scaling note).
limitations: Approximation only: duration and convexity alone summarize the curve (per source); large shifts and curve-shape changes escape it.
Assumes reinvestment at YTM and ignores richness/cheapness and financing effects (per source).

models.title: Levered portfolio return decomposition
models.summary: Levered return as invested return plus leverage-scaled excess over borrowing cost.

relationship.original_equation: rP = rI + (VB/VE)(rI − rB); equivalently rP = [rI(VE + VB) − VB·rB]/VE
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Using Leverage, printed p. 72 (PDF p. 82); Aschel solution 6.20% + (42/94.33)(6.20% − 2.80%) = 7.71%
relationship.translation_notes: Records the decomposed form (leverage effect isolated); the fractional form is the same identity rearranged. Decimal form. Dimensional check: dimensionless + (currency/currency × dimensionless) = dimensionless return.

models.title: Repo dollar interest (Actual/360)
models.summary: Repo interest as principal times rate times days over 360.

relationship.original_equation: Dollar interest = Principal amount × Repo rate × (Term of repo in days/360)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Repurchase Agreements, printed p. 73 (PDF p. 83); EUR15m × 5% × (1/360) = EUR2,083.33
relationship.translation_notes: 360 is the Actual/360 money-market day-count literal (pure arithmetic literal, not a unit conversion). Rate in decimal form (5% as 0.05); days is a dimensionless day count. Dimensional check: currency × dimensionless × (count/count) = currency interest.

variables.definition: Cash principal of the repo, in currency units
variables.context: same repo contract and term as r and days

variables.definition: Annualized repo rate, in decimal form (signed to admit negative-rate regimes)
variables.context: same repo contract and term as P and days

variables.definition: Term of the repo measured in days (dimensionless count, Actual leg of Actual/360)
variables.context: same repo contract as P and r

variables.definition: Repo interest amount (repurchase minus sale price), in the same currency units as P
variables.context: same repo contract as inputs
variables.domain: Finite signed interest (negative if rate negative)

assumptions: Actual/360 day-count convention and simple interest with no intra-term compounding (per corroborating source).
Single fixed term; rolled overnight repos reapply per roll.
limitations: Convention-specific: 365-day or other day-count regimes need their own literal (not recorded).
Haircuts affect fundable principal, not this interest arithmetic.
